name: Upham
description:
Perched in a high pass where a cloven falls becomes the source of two rivers in two separate valleys, Upham began as a mere wayside resting place for travelers and grew into a bustling center of trade for trappers and for merchants moving goods over the mountains.

The Upham General, its eight precarious stories of outfitters, smiths, taverns and lodgings embedded into the steep, crumbling mountainside, is the great hub of activity, with lesser establishments lining the roadway on either side. Squat, sturdy frames and broad roofs are shields that deflect the frequent falling boulders safely to either side and into the gorge below. Although travelers, merchants and other passers-through comprise the vast majority of souls in the town at any given time, a hardy and eclectic population of locals accumulates steadily year after year, their lives finding footholds amid the swift current of travelers.

A further population of trappers, trackers, hunters and explorers radiate out from Upham into the surrounding mountains. You'll see them in town, selling the spoils of their adventures and - often as not - spending the entirety of their gains that same night in the tavern at the General before trudging off into the wild again the next morning. If you can catch them during one of their brief sojourns, though, they will tell you of the strange and ancient shrines that dot the ridges and gorges of the mountains, how the whole region is teeming with spirits - some say gods - long forgotten but still powerful.

hooks.name: The Asana Commune
hooks.description:
On a high peak five days' march from Upham lie the ruins of what was once a place of great spiritual learning - the Asana Commune. For hundreds of years, pilgrims journeyed from far and wide to meditate on its terraces, stroll its airy gardens, and contemplate the world as they looked out over it through the high, thin air.

A century ago, a spirit attacked the Commune, tearing it apart and striking down any that stood in its way in an apparent search for something. Whatever it was looking for it did not find, for legend states that it returns each year, making the same destructive search and always leaving empty handed. The Commune lies now in ruins, efforts to rebuild it long-since abandoned under the annual onslaught.

What could the spirit be looking for?
hooks.gmNotes:
The spirit is Ikalā, the Lonely One - a powerful and ancient spirit of the mountains, about whom this legend is spoken:

"A century ago, a pilgrim was making her way to the Commune. She had been injured in a fall and her provisions were low when she encountered a man at a river crossing. The man showed her kindness, taking her to his home at a shrine nearby and nursing her back to health. They fell in love and she dwelt with him through the winter, postponing her pilgrimage.

In the spring she was with child, and the man revealed to her that he was Ikalā. He told her that their child would be born in the undying form of a spirit if she remained with him, but the child would be cursed with mortality if she left. Ikalā's deceit angered her, so she waited until he was away and then escaped, climbing to the Commune, where the meditants hid her from the strange man who frequently appeared, inquiring after her.

When the child was born in the Commune, dark clouds gathered and Ikalā appeared in wrath, no longer concealing his spirit form. His long, translucent black arms smashed the alabaster gates, tore apart the painted walls and scattered the monks' spheres in the courtyards.

The pilgrim, in a panic and still reeling from delivering the child, quickly hid the baby in a barrel of spices, before being crushed in the wreckage of the temples. When Ikalā began searching the spice barrels, the spices rose into the air and gave him such a sneezing fit that he gave up his search, carrying his wrath and sadness back down the mountain to his resting place.

What became of the child is unknown, but it is said that Ikalā still gives the spice barrels a wide berth in his annual searching. Thus are preserved there some of the world's rarest and most valuable spices - some of which are now gone from the earth."

Exactly when and where this legend reaches our Heroes' Ears is up to you, but hunters and trappers familiar with the area should warn them against going near to the ruins of the Commune, telling them that if you smell spices on the air, you should turn away.

Should they choose to go there anyway, they should indeed smell spices on the air as they approach. Getting closer, they should start finding cloth pouches of spices hung from branches and between pinnacles of the ruins.

It seems that Natsu, a scrawny rascal of a youth, has taken up residence in the ruins and has taken to placing spice-filled traps for Ikalā all around the place in an ever-widening perimeter of safe habitation. They are flippant about the threat of the great spirit, insisting that they can outsmart him and even fight him head on if they choose to. Their affect should be feral, their language broken, and their penchant for jests and pranks very great.

Natsu is, of course, the baby of the spice barrel, all grown up. But, it's been a hundred years and they seem to be a teenager. Their mixed parentage seems to have granted them neither typical mortality nor the immortality of the spirits, but a perpetual - or at least greatly prolonged - youth.

This should all remain hidden until Ikalā returns for his annual attack and search, during which Natsu's traps and defenses should fail and real mortal danger should confront them and Our Heroes, who must solve the riddle to reunite father and son - though it may not be a happy reunion.

hooks.name: Retaking Agland
hooks.description: Caelum, a humble dwarven blacksmith at the General, is descended from the Dwarves of Agland, a now-abandoned city under a mountain near Upham. The dwarves were "flushed out" of their home some fifty years ago by an unknown force. Caelum has vague dreams of reclaiming the city and its temple, but has found nobody willing to help him.
hooks.gmNotes:
Rumor of the hoards of Agland is well-known and often spoken of in Upham, but those who have tried to breach its gates have been driven back by fierce monsters that seem to feed on metal, turning it to rust.

Caelum is pious, fatalistic, chiefly interested in restoring the temple in Agland, and bristles at mention of the supposed treasure lying there for the taking. He has precious little practical knowledge to share about Agland: he was very young when the calamity occurred and his parents were loathe to speak of it out of shame. But he does remember a grand city in a huge underground chamber, and a great torrent of water crashing upon it.

It is three days' journey into the mountains to find the ancient entrance of Agland. Consider giving signs that the party is being followed. The entrance should give the immediate impression of the grand scale of the place. Perhaps some sort of puzzle to get the door to open.

Inside, Our Heroes find a variety of wonders and threats: the aforementioned metal-devouring monsters, a honeycomb city of stone, an army of mechanical servants, a "Hammer of Command" stuck in a hardened temple-pool of lava, a dormant volcano guarded by a sleeping goddess of craft, living stone guardians, a dripping passage leading to high chamber, where rests an ancient evil goddess of the sea, embryonic and floating in a giant sphere of hyper-dense seawater, and/or whatever else you care to include.

Who unleashed the torrent that flushed out the Dwarves? Why did they do it? Are they still there? Who, if anyone, followed Our Heroes? What do they want? What riches remain in Agland? Will Caelum part with them? What will happen if the temple is renewed? What does the Hammer of Command do?

hooks.name: A Mother's Anger
hooks.description: A hush comes over the tavern room at the Upham General. Something huge is walking on the road outside. The moon casts a massive shadow on the curtained windows, showing sharp fangs. A low growl shakes the tables. A moment of silence, then, an explosion of glass and timber as the beast crashes through the wall, swallowing three men in a single gulp. Even as carnage ensues, there is a desperation in the creature's eyes, which search the back of the room even as its claws rend flesh.
hooks.gmNotes: This is a sort of companion adventure that resonates with the Asana Commune adventure. It's simple enough - here we have a mother creature searching for its stolen young. The culprit is a trapper who caught her baby up in the mountains. She had tracked him here and will not rest until she has retrieved her baby and killed its captor.
